segments.he: פ"א הי' זקן א' מחשוביו של הבעש"ט ושמע ממנו שהוא יהי' לו נכד שיוכל לעשות טובה לבעל בחירה, ואחר פטירת הבעש"ט נסע לכל נכדי הבעש"ט לראות על מי כיוון הבעש"ט בדיבורו ולענין הבעל בחירה ובא אצל הרה"ק ר' ברוך ז"ל ושמע בעת שהי' בחוץ איך שהרה"ק מתאונן ואומר רבש"ע איך עושין טובה לבעל בחירה? ואמר הזקן א"כ ניט אייך מיינט איימהר זיידע וכו' וכשבא לרבינו ז"ל בחוץ שמע שרבינו ז"ל אמר בתנועה עמוקה כדרך תנועות רבינו ז"ל, "הן הבעל בחירה" כאומר אני יכול לעשות טובה לבעל בחירה ואמר הזקן עליכם כיוון זקינכם שתוכלו לעשות טובה לבעל בחירה. (א"ה להבין זאת הלא כל הצדיקים מתלמידי הבעש"ט היו עושין בעלי תשובה שהם בעלי בחירות אלא לעשות טובה לבעל בחירה מיט ציא נעמין צוא בחירה ורק לסעדו ולסמכו בעצות וכו' שהוא בעצמו יטה בחירתו לטוב ודווקא שיהא לו בחירה וזהו עיקר תשובת המשקל מ"ש זה לא הי' רק אצל רבינו ז"ל כי שאר הצדיקים עשו בעלי תשובה לקחו אותם על כתפם ולא החזירו להם הבחירה לילך שוב באלו המקומות שעברו וכו' ויש הרבה לדבר ולבאר בזה ולהראות בעליל שכן פ' אודל).
segments.en:
Concerning Reb Shimon, a disciple of Moharan'as [who was the grandfather of Reb Shimshon of Uman — named for him — whose gravestone stands together with that of Reb Naftali the disciple of Rabbainu, in the new cemetery in Uman]. He was a devoted disciple of Moharan'as and one of the most distinguished young men of his town. His father and family strongly opposed him and prevented him greatly from going to Moharan'as — and he paid them no attention whatsoever.

Once on Shabbos they took away his shoes and his outer garments — the kaplitsh and kaptan — so he could not go to Moharan'as for the third Shabbos meal. He was in great anguish and did not know what to do. His heart burned: how could he not be with Moharan'as? They had a thick coarse gentile garment. He put it on and went — without a hat, without shoes, wearing only the coarse gentile garment — to Moharan'as [it was summer]. He walked through the streets in this manner until he reached Moharan'as. And it goes without saying what humiliation and shame this was, since he was the most distinguished of the young men of his town.

When Moharan'as saw him in this condition, he understood what had happened. He said to him: "Es vet dir tsi, ves'l, kumen" [It will yet come to you, G-d willing]. And throughout his life he remained close to Moharan'as.

His companion Reb Avraham Ber — grandson of Rabbainu — told that after Reb Shimon's passing he saw him in a dream carrying a sack of stones on his shoulder. He asked: "What is this, and how has it been with you there?" He replied: When he passed away, he was not being judged and had not come to his rest — he was suffering greatly from this. He heard that through this place [a certain passage in the heavenly realms] disciples of Rabbainu were passing, and many souls ran to receive assistance. He ran with all his strength and reached that place. He saw Reb Shmuel Ayzik passing and begged him to help. Reb Shmuel Ayzik replied: "Shortly Reb Naftali will pass — perhaps he will help." When Reb Naftali passed he begged him too, and Reb Naftali replied: "Shortly Moharan'as will pass — he will certainly help you." And so it was: Moharan'as passed — and Reb Shimon wept before him, reminding him of how he had been among his close disciples, and of that Shabbos, and the words "It will yet come to you."

Moharan'as took him and led him to Rabbainu's Heichal [heavenly palace] — but they would not let him enter until he was first purified. For thirty days he was purified — then immersed in the River Dinur, the river of fire. At the first immersion he felt all the suffering in the world, and all his physicality and attachment to this world fell away. With the subsequent immersions he felt all the tastes and pleasures of Gan Eden. Afterward they admitted him to the Heichal — but there remained upon him the sin of being a debtor to Reb Avraham Ber, to whom he owed money — therefore he was walking about with the burden of stones upon his shoulder. He asked Reb Avraham Ber to forgive the debt. And so it was — he forgave him — and Reb Shimon came to his rest.
